questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) Psychologists call this asymmetry the self-serving bias.
(B) The same student, after scoring well, credits his own preparation.
(C) Effective feedback therefore points at method rather than at ability.
(D) Only when failure is attributed to something changeable does behaviour change.
(E) A student who fails a test often explains it by blaming the paper.
(F) It protects confidence in the short run and prevents learning in the long run.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (A) names 'this asymmetry', and sentence (F) evaluates the effects of the named bias with 'It', so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order E-B-A-F-D-C the pair A-F stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) They then need continuous air conditioning merely to remain habitable.
(B) The older builders were solving the same problem with no electricity at all.
(C) The design kept the interior cool through the hottest part of the afternoon.
(D) Traditional houses in Rajasthan were built with thick walls and small windows.
(E) Glass towers transplanted from colder climates reverse every one of those choices.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) describes the traditional construction, and sentence (C) explains the purpose of 'The design', so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order D-C-E-A-B the pair D-C stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?
(A) Mixing homes, shops and offices in the same block is the simplest remedy planners possess.
(B) The emptiness reinforces itself night after night.
(C) People on the pavement make the street feel safe to other people.
(D) A street lined with shops stays busy long after the offices have closed.
(E) Its pavements then feel unsafe, so fewer people use them.
(F) A district of office towers alone empties completely at seven in the evening.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) describes the busy mixed-use street and needs no earlier sentence, so it opens the passage. Sentence (C) explains why busy streets feel safe, which attaches it directly to the opening sentence. The complete order is D-C-F-E-B-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (E)?
(A) The following year two hours a week were blocked in the calendar for study.
(B) A company bought licences to an online course library for all its engineers.
(C) Completion rose to sixty per cent without a single new course being purchased.
(D) Learning was expected to happen after the day's delivery targets had been met.
(E) Completion rates after six months stood at four per cent.
(F) The courses were good; the difficulty was that nobody had been given time for them.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) reports the disappointing result, so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (B) opens with the company's purchase and provides it. Hence (B) immediately precedes (E), and the complete order is B-E-F-D-A-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which option correctly gives the FIRST and the LAST sentences of the paragraph, in that order?
(A) The difference in results looks like talent but begins as an assumption.
(B) Students who think this way stop attempting problems they cannot solve immediately.
(C) Many students believe mathematics is a subject you are either born for or not.
(D) Teaching that mistakes are part of the method changes the assumption, and with it the outcome.
(E) Those who treat difficulty as normal keep working and eventually succeed.
(F) That belief makes a wrong answer feel like evidence about the self.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) states the common belief and therefore opens the paragraph, while sentence (D) closes with the pedagogical conclusion and therefore closes it. The complete order is C-F-B-E-A-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) Surveys found that most residents lived more than two kilometres from any station.
(B) Planners expected the new stations to attract commuters from crowded buses.
(C) Ridership in the first year fell well below those projections.
(D) Ridership then rose to the level the original forecast had assumed.
(E) Walking that distance in the summer heat was not a realistic daily choice.
(F) A metro line was extended to a suburb that had grown rapidly for a decade.
(G) Feeder services connecting neighbourhoods to the stations were introduced the following year.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (D) reports the eventual outcome with 'then', which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (F) opens with the extension of the line. The full coherent order is F-B-C-A-E-G-D.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.
(A) Adding a buffer at the end of each phase absorbs the ordinary surprises.
(B) A schedule with no slack converts the first small delay into a crisis.
(C) Interruptions, however, are the one thing every project can count on.
(D) Project managers often use spreadsheets rather than specialised tools.
(E) Every project plan assumes that the work will proceed without interruption.
(F) The plan then survives contact with reality instead of being abandoned in week three.
questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (E) states the assumption built into plans; then the rest develop the same point in the order E-C-B-A-F. Sentence (D) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (3). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) A single striking experiment proves very little on its own. (2) Only when other laboratories obtain the same outcome does confidence grow. (3) Replication, unglamorous as it is, does most of the quiet work of science.
Removed sentence: Chance alone will produce an impressive result now and then.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence supports the claim by explaining the role of chance. It must therefore come after the sentence that states the opening claim about a single experiment and before the sentence that introduces the corrective step with 'Only when'. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: A single striking experiment proves very little on its own. Chance alone will produce an impressive result now and then. Only when other laboratories obtain the same outcome does confidence grow. Replication, unglamorous as it is, does most of the quiet work of science.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Analysts who skip this stage usually discover their mistake only when the results look absurd.
(B) Cleaning such records often consumes more time than building the model itself.
(C) Raw data collected from sensors is rarely ready for analysis.
(D) Readings may be missing, duplicated or recorded in different units.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (C) introduces raw sensor data as the subject. Sentence (D) specifies the defects in that data. Sentence (B) comments on the effort needed to clean 'such records'. Sentence (A) warns about skipping the stage and closes the paragraph. The coherent order is therefore C-D-B-A.

questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (F) introduces the survey question; then the rest develop the same point in the order F-G-C-D-A-B-E. questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (C)?
(A) Asking the most junior person to comment first changes the order of influence.
(B) Junior members in particular hesitate to contradict a senior who has already spoken.
(C) Agreement may mean that the difficult objection was never raised aloud.
(D) A meeting in which everyone agrees quickly is often a meeting that has failed.
(E) The objections that emerge then are the ones the team actually needed to hear.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) explains what the agreement may really mean. The sentence that continues this thread is (B), which identifies who stays silent and why. No other sentence links back to (C) so directly. The complete order is D-C-B-A-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which option correctly gives the FIRST and the LAST sentences of the paragraph, in that order?

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (A)?

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) This stream of readings lets the utility predict demand with far greater accuracy.
(B) A smart meter reports household electricity use to the utility every few minutes.
(C) It also reveals, inadvertently, when a family wakes up and when the house is empty.
(D) Rules on who may keep such records, and for how long, have not kept pace with the devices.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (B) introduces the smart meter and what it reports. Sentence (A) describes the benefit of 'This stream of readings'. Sentence (C) adds the privacy cost with 'It also reveals'. Sentence (D) concludes on the regulatory gap concerning 'such records'. The coherent order is therefore B-A-C-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (3). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) A cricket captain is judged almost entirely by results. (2) A bowling change that fails looks reckless, while the same change succeeding looks inspired. (3) Evaluating captaincy fairly means examining the reasoning rather than only the scoreboard.
Removed sentence: Yet the decisions that produce those results are made with incomplete information.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence qualifies that judgement with 'Yet'. It must therefore come after the sentence that opens with how captains are judged and before the sentence that illustrates the point with the bowling change. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: A cricket captain is judged almost entirely by results. Yet the decisions that produce those results are made with incomplete information. A bowling change that fails looks reckless, while the same change succeeding looks inspired. Evaluating captaincy fairly means examining the reasoning rather than only the scoreboard.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which option correctly gives the FIRST and the LAST sentences of the paragraph, in that order?

(B) During the peak season the springs cannot meet both local and visitor demand.
(C) The town's popularity ends up taxing precisely the people who made it worth visiting.
(D) Tankers then bring water up the hill at a price residents can hardly afford.
(E) A hill town that attracts visitors soon attracts hotels as well.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) opens the causal chain with visitors and hotels and therefore opens the paragraph, while sentence (C) sums up the irony as a closing sentence and therefore closes it. The complete order is E-A-B-D-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) Several firms have responded by switching off internal servers after a fixed hour.
(B) Remote working removed the daily commute for millions of employees.
(C) The hours saved were quickly absorbed by longer working days rather than by rest.
(D) Messages now arrive late at night because the office has no closing time.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (B) states the change brought about by remote work, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (C) reports what happened to 'The hours saved'. The full coherent order is B-C-D-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?
(A) Chance alone will produce an impressive result now and then.
(B) Replication, unglamorous as it is, does most of the quiet work of science.
(C) Only when other laboratories obtain the same outcome does confidence grow.
(D) A single striking experiment proves very little on its own.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) states the opening claim about a single experiment and needs no earlier sentence, so it opens the passage. Sentence (A) supports the claim by explaining the role of chance, which attaches it directly to the opening sentence. The complete order is D-A-C-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the CONCLUSION of the paragraph?
(A) A fair comparison of the two systems must count both the bin and the tap.
(B) The change cut its daily waste noticeably within a single week.
(C) Washing the mugs, however, raised the water used in the pantry.
(D) An office decided to replace its paper cups with ceramic mugs.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) introduces the offsetting cost with 'however', and sentence (A) states the balanced conclusion that follows from both effects, which settles the passage and leaves nothing hanging. Together they close the paragraph, whose full order is D-B-C-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the CONCLUSION of the paragraph?
(A) Hospitals now face infections that respond to only one or two remaining medicines.
(B) Antibiotics changed medicine by making once-fatal infections routinely curable.
(C) Bacteria exposed repeatedly to the same drugs gradually developed resistance to them.
(D) Their very success, however, encouraged doctors and patients to use them for minor complaints.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) describes the biological consequence of the overuse, and sentence (A) states the present-day situation that results from the chain of events, which settles the passage and leaves nothing hanging. Together they close the paragraph, whose full order is B-D-C-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the CONCLUSION of the paragraph?
(A) The older builders were solving the same problem with no electricity at all.
(B) Traditional houses in Rajasthan were built with thick walls and small windows.
(C) Glass towers transplanted from colder climates reverse every one of those choices.
(D) They then need continuous air conditioning merely to remain habitable.
(E) The design kept the interior cool through the hottest part of the afternoon.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) states the consequence for the towers with 'They then need', and sentence (A) closes with the comparison that makes the point, which settles the passage and leaves nothing hanging. Together they close the paragraph, whose full order is B-E-C-D-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Many began arriving at seven in the morning to find two quiet hours.
(B) A software firm moved its engineers into a single open hall to encourage collaboration.
(C) The collaboration the design intended had been replaced by elaborate avoidance.
(D) Conversation across desks did increase in the first few weeks.
(E) Engineers soon discovered that concentrated work had become almost impossible.
(F) Quiet rooms added later restored both the silence and, unexpectedly, the conversation.
(G) Others simply wore headphones and stopped responding to anyone nearby.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (B) opens with the firm's decision and its purpose. Sentence (D) reports the initial effect. Sentence (E) introduces the problem that engineers discovered. Sentence (A) describes the first coping strategy. Sentence (G) describes the second coping strategy with 'Others'. Sentence (C) summarises the irony of the outcome. Sentence (F) reports the later fix and its double benefit. The coherent order is therefore B-D-E-A-G-C-F.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (5). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) Concrete is strong when it is squeezed and weak when it is stretched. (2) Steel behaves in exactly the opposite way. (3) Reinforced concrete places steel bars precisely where the stretching occurs. (4) Corrosion of the hidden steel, however, is invisible until the surface cracks. (5) Inspection of old structures therefore concentrates on the material that cannot be seen.
Removed sentence: The two materials together carry loads that neither could carry alone.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence summarises the benefit of the combination. It must therefore come after the sentence that explains how reinforced concrete combines them and before the sentence that introduces the weakness with 'however'. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: Concrete is strong when it is squeezed and weak when it is stretched. Steel behaves in exactly the opposite way. Reinforced concrete places steel bars precisely where the stretching occurs. The two materials together carry loads that neither could carry alone. Corrosion of the hidden steel, however, is invisible until the surface cracks. Inspection of old structures therefore concentrates on the material that cannot be seen.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (F)?
(A) Those officers had rejected applicants from certain postal codes more often than others.
(B) The system learned the pattern faithfully and applied it at far greater speed.
(C) It surfaced only when auditors compared approval rates across neighbourhoods.
(D) An automated decision is therefore only as fair as the history it was taught from.
(E) A bank introduced an automated system to decide small personal loans.
(F) Because no rule mentioned the postal code explicitly, the bias was difficult to detect.
(G) The model was trained on a decade of decisions taken by human officers.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (F) explains why the bias was hard to detect. The sentence that continues this thread is (C), which describes how it was finally discovered with 'It surfaced only when'. No other sentence links back to (F) so directly. The complete order is E-G-A-B-F-C-D.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.
(A) If the tests still pass, the suite needs work before the product does.
(B) Real defects hide in the inputs nobody thought to write down.

(D) It may be checking only the cases the developer already had in mind.

questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (F) opens with the provocative claim about a suite that never fails; then the rest develop the same point in the order F-D-B-C-A. Sentence (E) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) They are lost between the field and the market rather than in the kitchen.
(B) Nearly a third of the vegetables grown in the country never reach a plate.

(D) Food waste in rural areas is therefore an energy problem disguised as an agricultural one.
(E) Such storage, however, requires reliable electricity in precisely the places that lack it.

questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (B) opens with the scale of the loss. Sentence (A) locates where the loss occurs. Sentence (C) describes the immediate cause. Sentence (F) proposes cold storage as the remedy. Sentence (E) introduces the obstacle with 'however'. Sentence (D) reframes the problem in the closing sentence. The coherent order is therefore B-A-C-F-E-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?

Sentence (B) opens with the observed problem, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (F) reports the first explanation and response. The full coherent order is B-F-A-E-D-C.

questions.questionText:

Sentence (E) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?

questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) states the seasonal pattern that the passage will explain and needs no earlier sentence, so it opens the passage. Sentence (A) identifies the cause behind that pattern, which attaches it directly to the opening sentence. The complete order is D-A-B-C.

questions.questionText:

Sentence (A) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (A)?
(A) Factories therefore automate the repetitive motion and leave the fiddly handling to people.
(B) Ask it to pick up a crumpled cloth, however, and it struggles badly.
(C) Tasks that humans find effortless often involve judgements no sensor captures easily.
(D) A robot arm can repeat the same weld ten thousand times without tiring.

questions.explanationText: Sentence (A) describes the practical division of labour with 'therefore', so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (C) explains the underlying reason and provides it. Hence (C) immediately precedes (A), and the complete order is D-B-C-A-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) A crowded protest can be made to look sparse by stepping two metres to the left.
(B) The image is accurate in every pixel and misleading all the same.
(C) A photograph records only what lies inside the frame.
(D) Everything the photographer chose to leave out is invisible to the viewer.
(E) Viewers judge pictures as evidence while forgetting that framing is an argument.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (C) states the basic fact about the frame. Sentence (D) points out the invisibility of what was excluded. Sentence (A) illustrates with the protest example. Sentence (B) evaluates that example with 'The image is accurate ... and misleading'. Sentence (E) closes with the general warning to viewers. The coherent order is therefore C-D-A-B-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (A)?
(A) Effective feedback therefore points at method rather than at ability.

(E) It protects confidence in the short run and prevents learning in the long run.
(F) Only when failure is attributed to something changeable does behaviour change.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (A) draws the practical conclusion about feedback, so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (F) states the condition under which behaviour changes and provides it. Hence (F) immediately precedes (A), and the complete order is B-D-C-E-F-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?

(B) The microwave oven began as an accident in a laboratory working on radar equipment.
(C) An engineer noticed that a chocolate bar in his pocket had melted near a magnetron.

Sentence (C) narrates the first observation, introducing the engineer, which attaches it directly to the opening sentence. The complete order is B-C-A-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (C)?
(A) Attackers then try it patiently against corporate systems until something opens.
(B) Most serious breaches begin not with clever code but with an ordinary stolen password.
(C) When any one of those services is compromised, the password becomes public.
(D) Even a correct password is useless without the second code sent to the user's device.
(E) Two-factor authentication breaks the chain at exactly this point.
(F) Employees reuse the same password across a dozen unrelated services.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) describes what happens when one service is compromised. The sentence that continues this thread is (A), which follows the attacker's next step with 'then'. No other sentence links back to (C) so directly. The complete order is B-F-C-A-E-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which option correctly gives the FIRST and the LAST sentences of the paragraph, in that order?

questions.questionText:

questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (D) presents the problem and introduces the subject of the paragraph. Sentence (B) proposes the better solution, which makes sense only after the easy option has been rejected. The coherent order is therefore D-C-A-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?

(E) Inspection of old structures therefore concentrates on the material that cannot be seen.
(F) Reinforced concrete places steel bars precisely where the stretching occurs.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (C) states concrete's property, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (D) states steel's opposite property. The full coherent order is C-D-F-B-A-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (B)?

(D) A correction printed on page fourteen cannot undo a headline printed on page one.
(E) Readers who saw the original rarely see the retraction.

Sentence (E) explains why by describing readers' behaviour and provides it. Hence (E) immediately precedes (B), and the complete order is D-E-B-C-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?

(D) An average conceals as much as it reveals.
(E) In the other, half the class is failing while the rest score full marks.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (B) introduces the two classes that illustrate it, and sentence (C) describes the first class with 'In one', so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order D-B-C-E-A the pair B-C stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (D)?

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?

questions.questionText:

questions.questionText:

questions.questionText:

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?
(A) The hours spent on precise drafting are therefore an insurance premium, not a formality.
(B) Vague wording that seemed harmless at signing becomes the whole dispute.
(C) Its clauses matter only when memory and goodwill have both run out.
(D) While relations are cordial, nobody consults the document at all.
(E) A contract is written mainly for the day the parties stop agreeing.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) states the purpose of a contract and needs no earlier sentence, so it opens the passage. Sentence (D) describes what happens while relations are good, which attaches it directly to the opening sentence. The complete order is E-D-C-B-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) Each half then breeds only within itself.
(B) Monitoring cameras in Karnataka have recorded elephants using such crossings within months.
(C) Over generations the smaller gene pools make both groups more vulnerable to disease.
(D) A highway cutting through a forest divides one animal population into two.
(E) Underpasses and canopy bridges restore the movement the road removed.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (D) states the effect of the highway, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (A) describes the breeding consequence with 'Each half then'. The full coherent order is D-A-C-E-B.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.
(A) A model that performs perfectly on its training data is not necessarily a good model.
(B) Only the score on that unseen portion tells them how the system will behave in the field.
(C) Such a model collapses as soon as it meets a case that differs slightly from the training set.
(D) Deep networks require far more computation than linear regression.
(E) It may simply have memorised the examples it was shown, including their noise.
(F) Practitioners guard against this by holding back a portion of the data for testing.
questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (A) makes the opening claim about training accuracy; then the rest develop the same point in the order A-E-C-F-B. Sentence (D) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (C)?
(A) As renewable generation grows, however, the same car becomes cleaner without any change to it.
(B) In a grid dominated by coal, the saving is therefore smaller than the silence suggests.
(C) Its environmental record is tied less to the vehicle than to the grid behind it.
(D) An electric car produces no exhaust on the street where it is driven.
(E) The emissions associated with it occur instead at the power station that charges it.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) states the general principle that unites both cases, so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (A) introduces the opposite case with 'however' and provides it. Hence (A) immediately precedes (C), and the complete order is D-E-B-A-C.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.
(A) A forgotten test machine can quietly bill a company for months.
(B) Fibre optic cables carry most intercontinental internet traffic.
(C) This flexibility, however, makes costs much harder to predict than a one-time purchase.
(D) Running a service in the cloud removes the need to buy and house physical servers.
(E) Capacity can be increased for a single busy weekend and released on Monday morning.
(F) Most teams therefore set spending alerts before they set performance targets.
questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (D) states the basic advantage of the cloud; then the rest develop the same point in the order D-E-C-A-F. Sentence (B) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Recovery produces no number that can be posted on a noticeboard.
(B) Athletes consequently train hard and sleep badly, undoing much of the gain.
(C) Training plans, however, concentrate almost entirely on the first of these.
(D) Coaches who schedule rest as carefully as they schedule repetitions see the difference within a season.
(E) A sprinter's performance depends on power, technique and recovery in roughly equal measure.
(F) Power is easy to measure and improves visibly within weeks.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (E) states the three factors that matter. Sentence (C) points out the imbalance in training plans with 'however'. Sentence (F) explains why power dominates. Sentence (A) contrasts recovery, which produces no number. Sentence (B) describes the consequence for athletes. Sentence (D) closes with what better coaches do. The coherent order is therefore E-C-F-A-B-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the CONCLUSION of the paragraph?
(A) Teachers insist instead on slow repetition until the movement is exactly right.
(B) Speed, however, only repeats the mistakes already present in the fingers.
(C) A beginner practises a difficult passage by playing it faster and faster.
(D) Tempo, added afterwards, costs far less effort than correction does.
(E) The hand then learns one version of the passage rather than several competing ones.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) explains the benefit with 'The hand then learns', and sentence (D) closes with the comparison between adding tempo and correcting errors, which settles the passage and leaves nothing hanging. Together they close the paragraph, whose full order is C-B-A-E-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) In practice, one or two members often complete most of the task themselves.
(B) The others learn that silence costs them nothing at all.
(C) Group projects are meant to teach students how to divide work and negotiate deadlines.
(D) Grading individual contributions, not just the final report, removes much of that incentive.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (B) describes what 'The others' take away from the experience, and sentence (D) proposes the fix, which only makes sense after the incentive has been described, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order C-A-B-D the pair B-D stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) Removing a feature, however, angers the small group that depends on it.
(B) Together, they produce a product whose settings page nobody can navigate.
(C) Every system acquires features faster than it acquires the capacity to support them.
(D) The hidden complexity remains, waiting to surface as the next maintenance problem.
(E) Teams therefore keep everything and hide the complexity behind defaults.
(F) Each addition seems harmless when considered on its own.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (C) states the general tendency of systems, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (F) explains why each addition is accepted. The full coherent order is C-F-B-A-E-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) Car owners, meanwhile, continued to drive exactly as before.
(B) Ridership rose sharply within the first month.
(C) A city announced free bus travel for all its residents.
(D) Making buses faster, rather than cheaper, would have targeted the drivers the city wanted to attract.
(E) Congestion therefore remained unchanged while the fare revenue disappeared.
(F) Most of the new passengers, surveys showed, had previously walked or cycled.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) opens with the policy decision, and sentence (B) reports the immediate effect on ridership, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order C-B-F-A-E-D the pair C-B stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) Two-factor authentication breaks the chain at exactly this point.
(B) Attackers then try it patiently against corporate systems until something opens.
(C) Even a correct password is useless without the second code sent to the user's device.
(D) When any one of those services is compromised, the password becomes public.
(E) Most serious breaches begin not with clever code but with an ordinary stolen password.
(F) Employees reuse the same password across a dozen unrelated services.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (E) opens with the claim about how breaches begin, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (F) explains the employee habit behind it. The full coherent order is E-F-D-B-A-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (E)?
(A) Ask it to pick up a crumpled cloth, however, and it struggles badly.
(B) Factories therefore automate the repetitive motion and leave the fiddly handling to people.
(C) Tasks that humans find effortless often involve judgements no sensor captures easily.
(D) The result is a shared workspace rather than the empty factory once predicted.
(E) A robot arm can repeat the same weld ten thousand times without tiring.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) states what the robot does well. The sentence that continues this thread is (A), which contrasts with the difficult task using 'however'. No other sentence links back to (E) so directly. The complete order is E-A-C-B-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) It therefore reproduces the habits, and also the prejudices, of the text it was trained on.
(B) Correcting such tendencies requires careful curation of the training material rather than clever programming alone.
(C) A system trained mostly on documents written by men may describe engineers as 'he' by default.
(D) A language model learns by predicting the next word in enormous amounts of text.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (D) explains how the model learns and introduces the subject. Sentence (A) uses 'It therefore' to draw the immediate consequence of that learning method. Sentence (C) gives a concrete example of the prejudice described. Sentence (B) states what the correction demands and concludes. The coherent order is therefore D-A-C-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (C)?
(A) Shoppers, however, rarely eat exactly a hundred grams of anything.
(B) The number that matters is therefore energy per packet, not energy per hundred grams.
(C) Some regulators now require both figures to be printed side by side.
(D) A food label lists the energy in a hundred grams of the product.
(E) A packet of biscuits that looks modest on the label may contain three such portions.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) reports the regulatory response and closes, so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (B) states the conclusion that follows with 'therefore' and provides it. Hence (B) immediately precedes (C), and the complete order is D-A-E-B-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (B)?
(A) No individual farmer gains by stopping while the others continue.
(B) A borewell deepened by fifty metres yields water again within a week.
(C) The relief lasts only until the neighbouring farmer deepens his own.
(D) Each extra metre lowers the shared water table a little further.
(E) Only an agreement covering the whole aquifer can break the race downward.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (B) opens with the individual action and its immediate effect. The sentence that continues this thread is (C), which reports how briefly 'The relief' lasts. No other sentence links back to (B) so directly. The complete order is B-C-D-A-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which option correctly gives the FIRST and the LAST sentences of the paragraph, in that order?
(A) Many began arriving at seven in the morning to find two quiet hours.
(B) Others simply wore headphones and stopped responding to anyone nearby.
(C) Quiet rooms added later restored both the silence and, unexpectedly, the conversation.
(D) Conversation across desks did increase in the first few weeks.
(E) A software firm moved its engineers into a single open hall to encourage collaboration.
(F) Engineers soon discovered that concentrated work had become almost impossible.
(G) The collaboration the design intended had been replaced by elaborate avoidance.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) opens with the firm's decision and its purpose and therefore opens the paragraph, while sentence (C) reports the later fix and its double benefit and therefore closes it. The complete order is E-D-F-A-B-G-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (F)?
(A) It protects confidence in the short run and prevents learning in the long run.
(B) Psychologists call this asymmetry the self-serving bias.
(C) The same student, after scoring well, credits his own preparation.
(D) Effective feedback therefore points at method rather than at ability.
(E) Only when failure is attributed to something changeable does behaviour change.
(F) A student who fails a test often explains it by blaming the paper.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (F) gives the first half of the observed asymmetry. The sentence that continues this thread is (C), which gives the second half using 'The same student'. No other sentence links back to (F) so directly. The complete order is F-C-B-A-E-D.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (4). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) Free delivery is never actually free for the company that offers it. (2) The cost is folded into the price of the goods or absorbed from the margin. (3) Shoppers nevertheless respond far more strongly to a zero shipping fee than to a lower price. (4) The arithmetic is identical; only the framing has changed.
Removed sentence: An item at 499 rupees with free delivery outsells the same item at 449 rupees plus 50 for delivery.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence gives the numerical illustration. It must therefore come after the sentence that reports the shopper's reaction with 'nevertheless' and before the sentence that closes by naming the difference as framing. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: Free delivery is never actually free for the company that offers it. The cost is folded into the price of the goods or absorbed from the margin. Shoppers nevertheless respond far more strongly to a zero shipping fee than to a lower price. An item at 499 rupees with free delivery outsells the same item at 449 rupees plus 50 for delivery. The arithmetic is identical; only the framing has changed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the CONCLUSION of the paragraph?
(A) Anonymity is therefore a property of the whole collection, not of any one field.
(B) Organisations that strip names and consider the job finished are mistaken.
(C) A single piece of anonymous data usually reveals nothing about a person.
(D) Genuine protection requires limiting how finely the remaining details can be combined.
(E) Combine a postal code, a date of birth and a gender, however, and most individuals become identifiable.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (B) applies it to organisations that only remove names, and sentence (D) states what genuine protection requires, which settles the passage and leaves nothing hanging. Together they close the paragraph, whose full order is C-E-A-B-D.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.
(A) Its value lies not in sounding plausible but in being capable of failing a test.
(B) This is why astrologers, who can explain every outcome after the event, persuade so few scientists.
(C) A hypothesis is a testable statement about how something in the world behaves.
(D) If no observation could possibly contradict a claim, the claim lies outside science.
(E) Telescopes have grown steadily larger since Galileo's time.
questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (C) defines the key term and must stand first; then the rest develop the same point in the order C-A-D-B. Sentence (E) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (E)?
(A) Deliberately introducing a fault and watching whether the suite notices is a useful audit.
(B) A test suite that never fails is usually telling you nothing.
(C) Real defects hide in the inputs nobody thought to write down.
(D) If the tests still pass, the suite needs work before the product does.
(E) It may be checking only the cases the developer already had in mind.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) explains the reason using 'It may be checking'. The sentence that continues this thread is (C), which states where real defects actually hide. No other sentence links back to (E) so directly. The complete order is B-E-C-A-D.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (5). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) A seed company promised a variety of wheat that would yield a third more grain. (2) The promise was honest, but it assumed irrigation at two fixed points in the season. (3) Farmers who had canal water obtained the yields that had been advertised. (4) Those depending on rainfall harvested less than they had with their old seed. (5) Advice that travels with the seed matters as much as the seed itself.
Removed sentence: The variety was not a fraud; it was simply unsuited to half its buyers.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence evaluates the variety in the light of both groups. It must therefore come after the sentence that contrasts the outcome for rain-fed farmers and before the sentence that states the general lesson as a conclusion. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: A seed company promised a variety of wheat that would yield a third more grain. The promise was honest, but it assumed irrigation at two fixed points in the season. Farmers who had canal water obtained the yields that had been advertised. Those depending on rainfall harvested less than they had with their old seed. The variety was not a fraud; it was simply unsuited to half its buyers. Advice that travels with the seed matters as much as the seed itself.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) The readings showed that he had been watering the crop twice as often as it needed.
(B) A farmer in Vidarbha installed soil moisture sensors in two of his cotton fields.
(C) After he adjusted the schedule, his pump ran for half the earlier number of hours.
(D) His neighbours, seeing the lower electricity bills, asked to borrow the sensors the following season.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (B) opens the narrative with the farmer and his action. Sentence (A) reports what 'The readings' revealed. Sentence (C) describes the change made after the discovery. Sentence (D) concludes with the effect on the neighbours. The coherent order is therefore B-A-C-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (B)?
(A) The relief lasts only until the neighbouring farmer deepens his own.
(B) Only an agreement covering the whole aquifer can break the race downward.
(C) No individual farmer gains by stopping while the others continue.
(D) Each extra metre lowers the shared water table a little further.
(E) A borewell deepened by fifty metres yields water again within a week.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (B) concludes with the collective solution, so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (C) states why individual restraint fails and provides it. Hence (C) immediately precedes (B), and the complete order is E-A-D-C-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?
(A) The original authors issued a clarification that attracted almost no attention.
(B) The gap between a cell culture and a patient is where most promising findings quietly disappear.
(C) A laboratory reported that a common spice slowed the growth of cancer cells.
(D) Readers began consuming it in quantities no study had ever examined.
(E) Doses that work in a dish often fail entirely once digestion and circulation intervene.
(F) Newspapers nevertheless announced that the spice fought cancer.
(G) The experiment had been carried out on cells in a dish, not in a living body.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) reports the laboratory finding and needs no earlier sentence, so it opens the passage. Sentence (G) states the crucial limitation of 'The experiment', which attaches it directly to the opening sentence. The complete order is C-G-F-D-A-E-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) A record therefore accumulates of every place the user visits, running or not.
(B) Operating systems have begun asking again after a few weeks of background use.
(C) The same permission, once granted, continues to apply when the application is idle.
(D) A fitness application asks for access to a user's location in order to map runs.
(E) Most users never revisit the permission screen after the first day.
(F) The repeated question restores a choice that the original consent quietly removed.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (D) introduces the application and the permission it requests. Sentence (C) explains what 'The same permission' covers afterwards. Sentence (A) states the consequence with 'therefore'. Sentence (E) notes the user behaviour that makes it worse. Sentence (B) describes the response from operating systems. Sentence (F) explains why the response matters and closes. The coherent order is therefore D-C-A-E-B-F.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Manufacturers assumed that ordinary households would never need one.
(B) Handsets were redesigned around a function the designers had considered trivial.
(C) The first mobile phones were marketed as tools for business travellers.
(D) Teenagers, not executives, became the users who drove the next wave of sales.
(E) Text messaging, added almost as an afterthought by engineers, turned out to be the feature they wanted.
(F) The market, as so often, decided what the product was actually for.
(G) Prices fell faster than anyone in the industry had predicted.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (C) opens with the original positioning of mobile phones. Sentence (A) states the manufacturers' assumption. Sentence (G) introduces the unexpected fall in prices. Sentence (D) identifies the users who actually drove sales. Sentence (E) explains which feature they wanted. Sentence (B) describes how handsets were redesigned as a result. Sentence (F) closes with the general reflection. The coherent order is therefore C-A-G-D-E-B-F.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) This is why astrologers, who can explain every outcome after the event, persuade so few scientists.
(B) If no observation could possibly contradict a claim, the claim lies outside science.
(C) Its value lies not in sounding plausible but in being capable of failing a test.
(D) A hypothesis is a testable statement about how something in the world behaves.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (D) defines the key term and must stand first. Sentence (C) comments on the value of the hypothesis using 'Its'. Sentence (B) generalises the point about testability. Sentence (A) begins with 'This is why' and offers the illustrative case. The coherent order is therefore D-C-B-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) Enjoying it, they read more books and widen the gap further.
(B) The child who struggled at the start reads less and falls steadily behind.
(C) That head start makes early lessons easier, so they enjoy reading more.
(D) Children who are read to before school begins arrive with a larger vocabulary.
(E) Researchers call this widening of an initial difference the Matthew effect.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (E) names the whole pattern and closes the paragraph, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (D) states the initial advantage. The full coherent order is D-C-A-B-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (E)?
(A) Books can describe the sequence of steps but not the feel of the material.
(B) Rebuilding it has taken decades where the last experienced hands had already retired.
(C) A craft is learned by watching somebody who is better at it than you are.
(D) Industries that lost their apprenticeship systems found the knowledge impossible to document afterwards.
(E) An apprentice absorbs that judgement slowly, through correction rather than instruction.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) describes how the apprentice acquires 'that judgement'. The sentence that continues this thread is (D), which reports what happened where apprenticeships disappeared. No other sentence links back to (E) so directly. The complete order is C-A-E-D-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) New construction shifted to segments the rules did not cover.
(B) A city introduced rent control to keep older neighbourhoods affordable.
(C) Existing tenants benefited immediately and many stayed for decades.
(D) Who benefits from a price rule depends almost entirely on who already holds the asset.
(E) Families arriving in the city found almost nothing available to rent at all.
(F) Owners, unable to raise rents, spent less on maintenance each year.
(G) The policy protected those already inside while raising the barrier for everyone outside.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (D) states the general conclusion, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (B) opens with the policy and its intention. The full coherent order is B-C-F-A-E-G-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) It therefore reproduces the habits, and also the prejudices, of the text it was trained on.
(B) A language model learns by predicting the next word in enormous amounts of text.
(C) Correcting such tendencies requires careful curation of the training material rather than clever programming alone.

questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (C) states what the correction demands and concludes, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (B) explains how the model learns and introduces the subject. The full coherent order is B-A-D-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Canal companies cut their tolls, then sold their waterways to the railways themselves.
(B) Once the network joined major cities, however, the advantage reversed completely.
(C) A technology built as a supplement had absorbed the system it was meant to serve.
(D) Canals carried most heavy freight in Britain before the railways arrived.
(E) They were slow, but nothing cheaper existed for moving coal and iron.
(F) The first railway lines were built to feed the canals rather than to replace them.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (D) sets the historical scene before railways. Sentence (E) explains why canals were used despite being slow. Sentence (F) describes the original purpose of early railways. Sentence (B) marks the turning point with 'however'. Sentence (A) narrates the response of the canal companies. Sentence (C) closes with the summarising reflection. The coherent order is therefore D-E-F-B-A-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Reinforced concrete places steel bars precisely where the stretching occurs.
(B) Steel behaves in exactly the opposite way.
(C) Concrete is strong when it is squeezed and weak when it is stretched.
(D) Corrosion of the hidden steel, however, is invisible until the surface cracks.
(E) Inspection of old structures therefore concentrates on the material that cannot be seen.
(F) The two materials together carry loads that neither could carry alone.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (C) states concrete's property. Sentence (B) states steel's opposite property. Sentence (A) explains how reinforced concrete combines them. Sentence (F) summarises the benefit of the combination. Sentence (D) introduces the weakness with 'however'. Sentence (E) draws the conclusion about inspection. The coherent order is therefore C-B-A-F-D-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) Their first customers were friends who shared photographs of the bags online.
(B) Within two years the room had become a small workshop employing eleven artisans.
(C) Those photographs brought orders from cities the founders had never visited.

Sentence (A) reports the failure of that response. Sentence (E) introduces the second strategy with 'then'. Sentence (B) describes what customers did in response. Sentence (F) states the conclusion drawn from the comparison. The coherent order is therefore D-C-A-E-B-F.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Replication, unglamorous as it is, does most of the quiet work of science.
(B) Only when other laboratories obtain the same outcome does confidence grow.
(C) A single striking experiment proves very little on its own.
(D) Chance alone will produce an impressive result now and then.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (C) states the opening claim about a single experiment. Sentence (D) supports the claim by explaining the role of chance. Sentence (B) introduces the corrective step with 'Only when'. Sentence (A) names and evaluates that step as a closing generalisation. The coherent order is therefore C-D-B-A.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.
(A) Sensors have become remarkably cheap in the past decade.
(B) Analysts who skip this stage usually discover their mistake only when the results look absurd.
(C) Readings may be missing, duplicated or recorded in different units.
(D) Cleaning such records often consumes more time than building the model itself.
(E) Raw data collected from sensors is rarely ready for analysis.
questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (E) introduces raw sensor data as the subject; then the rest develop the same point in the order E-C-D-B. Sentence (A) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) It is picked up in corridor conversations, review meetings and casual lunchtime remarks.

(C) A new employee usually spends the first few weeks simply learning how decisions are made.
(D) Teams that ignore this hidden curriculum often wonder why capable recruits take so long to contribute.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (C) introduces the new employee and the period of learning, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (B) describes the nature of that knowledge through 'this knowledge'. The full coherent order is C-B-A-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the CONCLUSION of the paragraph?
(A) That belief makes a wrong answer feel like evidence about the self.
(B) Students who think this way stop attempting problems they cannot solve immediately.
(C) The difference in results looks like talent but begins as an assumption.
(D) Many students believe mathematics is a subject you are either born for or not.
(E) Those who treat difficulty as normal keep working and eventually succeed.
(F) Teaching that mistakes are part of the method changes the assumption, and with it the outcome.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) interprets the resulting difference, and sentence (F) closes with the pedagogical conclusion, which settles the passage and leaves nothing hanging. Together they close the paragraph, whose full order is D-A-B-E-C-F.

questions.questionText:
