questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (D)?
(A) Its accuracy drops, however, when it is shown films from a scanner of a different make.
(B) The machine has partly learned the quirks of the equipment rather than the signs of disease.
(C) Before any such tool is deployed, it must therefore be tested on the hospital's own images.
(D) On the images it has seen before, it matches expert performance comfortably.
(E) Hospitals have begun using software that reads chest X-rays and flags suspicious shadows.
(F) The system was trained on hundreds of thousands of images already labelled by radiologists.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) reports its performance on familiar images, so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (F) explains how 'The system' was trained and provides it. Hence (F) immediately precedes (D), and the complete order is E-F-D-A-B-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) A student who can reproduce a sorting algorithm on paper may still be unable to debug a simple program.
(B) This method rewards memory far more than it rewards the ability to build something that works.
(C) Several institutions have therefore begun to add project reviews and code walkthroughs to their evaluation schemes.
(D) Most engineering colleges still assess students mainly through written examinations.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (D) states the existing practice in neutral, general terms and needs no earlier sentence. Sentence (B) comments on that practice using 'This method', which must point back to the examination system. Sentence (A) illustrates the weakness with a concrete student example. Sentence (C) begins with 'therefore' and reports the corrective step that follows from the problem. The coherent order is therefore D-B-A-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the CONCLUSION of the paragraph?
(A) The reform succeeded for the learners and failed for the staff who had to sustain it.
(B) Students reported less anxiety than they had felt before the single long paper.
(C) Any change to assessment must therefore be costed in teacher hours before it is announced.
(D) Attendance improved immediately, since each test carried marks.
(E) Teachers, however, found themselves setting and marking four times as often.
(F) A college replaced its three-hour final examination with four short tests spread across the term.
(G) Several reused questions, and the papers soon began to circulate among students.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (A) evaluates the reform from both sides, and sentence (C) states the general principle that closes the passage, which settles the passage and leaves nothing hanging. Together they close the paragraph, whose full order is F-D-B-E-G-A-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) Flexibility on the consumption side is thus cheaper than flexibility on the generation side.
(B) Electricity cannot be stored in the wires themselves.
(C) This reserve costs money even on days when it is never used.
(D) Operators therefore keep spare plants running below capacity, ready to increase output.
(E) Demand that can be shifted, such as charging or pumping, reduces the reserve required.
(F) A power grid must match generation to consumption second by second.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (F) states the fundamental requirement of a grid, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (B) explains why with the fact about storage. The full coherent order is F-B-D-C-E-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) A typical message warns that an account will be closed unless the user verifies it immediately.
(B) The attacker's aim is to make the reader reveal a password or click a harmful link.
(C) Because the warning creates panic, even careful employees sometimes respond without checking the sender's address.
(D) Phishing is an attack in which a fraudulent message is disguised as a trustworthy one.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) defines the term 'phishing' and so must come first, and sentence (B) explains the attacker's purpose and refers back to 'the attacker' introduced by the definition, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order D-B-A-C the pair D-B stands together.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (3). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) A recommendation engine studies what a user has already watched or bought. (2) From that history it predicts which items the same user is likely to choose next. (3) This is why a new account receives rather generic suggestions during its first few days.
Removed sentence: The predictions improve as more data accumulates, since patterns become easier to detect.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence adds how the mechanism improves over time. It must therefore come after the sentence that continues the mechanism with 'From that history', which depends on the previous sentence and before the sentence that begins with 'This is why' and draws the consequence for a new account. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: A recommendation engine studies what a user has already watched or bought. From that history it predicts which items the same user is likely to choose next. The predictions improve as more data accumulates, since patterns become easier to detect. This is why a new account receives rather generic suggestions during its first few days.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (C)?
(A) Genuine protection requires limiting how finely the remaining details can be combined.
(B) A single piece of anonymous data usually reveals nothing about a person.
(C) Combine a postal code, a date of birth and a gender, however, and most individuals become identifiable.
(D) Anonymity is therefore a property of the whole collection, not of any one field.
(E) Organisations that strip names and consider the job finished are mistaken.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) introduces the combination with 'however'. The sentence that continues this thread is (D), which draws the general conclusion with 'therefore'. No other sentence links back to (C) so directly. The complete order is B-C-D-E-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) This mismatch leaves cheap afternoon electricity with nowhere useful to go.
(B) Household demand, by contrast, peaks in the evening when people return home.
(C) Solar panels generate most of their power in the middle of the day.
(D) Storage, whether in batteries or in pumped water, shifts the surplus to the evening.
(E) The cost of that shift, rather than the cost of the panel, now decides the economics.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (C) states when solar power is produced. Sentence (B) contrasts it with demand using 'by contrast'. Sentence (A) names the resulting problem as 'This mismatch'. Sentence (D) introduces storage as the solution. Sentence (E) closes with the economic conclusion about 'that shift'. The coherent order is therefore C-B-A-D-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) Capital raised after those conversations buys far more than capital raised before them.
(B) Investment, however, buys speed rather than direction.
(C) A company that does not yet know its customer simply reaches the wrong market faster.
(D) The months before funding are the cheapest time to discover a mistake.
(E) Each conversation with a potential buyer costs nothing and eliminates a wrong assumption.
(F) A founder with a working prototype is usually advised to raise money quickly.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) points to the value of the pre-funding months, and sentence (E) explains why with the cost of each conversation, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order F-B-C-D-E-A the pair D-E stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) It explains why candidates interviewed first or last are often recalled most clearly.
(B) People remember the beginning and the end of an experience far better than its middle.
(C) Experienced panels therefore take detailed notes rather than trusting their memory of the day.
(D) Researchers describe this tendency as the serial position effect.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (B) states the general observation about memory, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (D) supplies the technical name for 'this tendency'. The full coherent order is B-D-A-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which option correctly gives the FIRST and the LAST sentences of the paragraph, in that order?
(A) Messages now arrive late at night because the office has no closing time.
(B) The hours saved were quickly absorbed by longer working days rather than by rest.
(C) Remote working removed the daily commute for millions of employees.
(D) Several firms have responded by switching off internal servers after a fixed hour.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) states the change brought about by remote work and therefore opens the paragraph, while sentence (D) reports the organisational response, which can only follow the problem and therefore closes it. The complete order is C-B-A-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Making buses faster, rather than cheaper, would have targeted the drivers the city wanted to attract.
(B) A city announced free bus travel for all its residents.
(C) Most of the new passengers, surveys showed, had previously walked or cycled.
(D) Ridership rose sharply within the first month.
(E) Car owners, meanwhile, continued to drive exactly as before.
(F) Congestion therefore remained unchanged while the fare revenue disappeared.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (B) opens with the policy decision. Sentence (D) reports the immediate effect on ridership. Sentence (C) reveals who the new passengers were. Sentence (E) contrasts the behaviour of car owners with 'meanwhile'. Sentence (F) states the combined outcome with 'therefore'. Sentence (A) closes with the alternative policy that would have worked. The coherent order is therefore B-D-C-E-F-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which option correctly gives the FIRST and the LAST sentences of the paragraph, in that order?
(A) Those depending on rainfall harvested less than they had with their old seed.
(B) Farmers who had canal water obtained the yields that had been advertised.
(C) The promise was honest, but it assumed irrigation at two fixed points in the season.
(D) The variety was not a fraud; it was simply unsuited to half its buyers.
(E) Advice that travels with the seed matters as much as the seed itself.
(F) A seed company promised a variety of wheat that would yield a third more grain.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (F) opens with the company's promise and therefore opens the paragraph, while sentence (E) states the general lesson as a conclusion and therefore closes it. The complete order is F-C-B-A-D-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) A bowling change that fails looks reckless, while the same change succeeding looks inspired.
(B) Yet the decisions that produce those results are made with incomplete information.
(C) A cricket captain is judged almost entirely by results.
(D) Evaluating captaincy fairly means examining the reasoning rather than only the scoreboard.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (C) opens with how captains are judged. Sentence (B) qualifies that judgement with 'Yet'. Sentence (A) illustrates the point with the bowling change. Sentence (D) offers the concluding recommendation. The coherent order is therefore C-B-A-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?

questions.questionText:

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?

(B) His neighbours, seeing the lower electricity bills, asked to borrow the sensors the following season.

questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) opens the narrative with the farmer and his action and needs no earlier sentence, so it opens the passage. Sentence (A) reports what 'The readings' revealed, which attaches it directly to the opening sentence. The complete order is D-A-C-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) Power is easy to measure and improves visibly within weeks.
(B) Coaches who schedule rest as carefully as they schedule repetitions see the difference within a season.
(C) Athletes consequently train hard and sleep badly, undoing much of the gain.
(D) A sprinter's performance depends on power, technique and recovery in roughly equal measure.
(E) Training plans, however, concentrate almost entirely on the first of these.
(F) Recovery produces no number that can be posted on a noticeboard.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (B) closes with what better coaches do, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (D) states the three factors that matter. The full coherent order is D-E-A-F-C-B.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (5). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?

Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: A fitness application asks for access to a user's location in order to map runs. The same permission, once granted, continues to apply when the application is idle. A record therefore accumulates of every place the user visits, running or not. Most users never revisit the permission screen after the first day. Operating systems have begun asking again after a few weeks of background use. An engineer noticed that a chocolate bar in his pocket had melted near a magnetron. Curious about the cause, he placed popcorn kernels in front of the device and watched them burst. questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?

(B) Adapting the city, not merely predicting the storm, has become the urgent task.

(D) Drainage built for the older pattern is overwhelmed within an hour of such a burst.
(E) A warmer atmosphere holds more water vapour than a cooler one.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?

questions.questionText:

Sentence (D) closes with the planning remedy, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (B) describes the busy mixed-use street. The full coherent order is B-A-C-F-E-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (D)?
(A) The arrangement fails, though, when nobody is responsible for accepting the corrections.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Books can describe the sequence of steps but not the feel of the material.
(B) Rebuilding it has taken decades where the last experienced hands had already retired.
(C) Industries that lost their apprenticeship systems found the knowledge impossible to document afterwards.
(D) An apprentice absorbs that judgement slowly, through correction rather than instruction.
(E) A craft is learned by watching somebody who is better at it than you are.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (E) states how a craft is learned. Sentence (A) explains the limitation of books. Sentence (D) describes how the apprentice acquires 'that judgement'. Sentence (C) reports what happened where apprenticeships disappeared. Sentence (B) closes with the cost of rebuilding. The coherent order is therefore E-A-D-C-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) Only four of the school's fifteen machines actually worked.
(B) Attendance doubled once the lessons matched the equipment that existed.
(C) A college club began teaching basic computer skills in a nearby municipal school.
(D) The first sessions failed because the volunteers prepared lessons for an empty laboratory.
(E) The students redesigned the course around pairs sharing a single computer.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (A) explains the reason by describing the machines, and sentence (E) describes the redesign that followed the discovery, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order C-D-A-E-B the pair A-E stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) A company that measures only the complaints it receives will therefore see a flattering picture.
(B) Surveys of lapsed buyers usually reveal problems that the complaint register never recorded.
(C) Customers rarely complain about a product that merely disappoints them.
(D) They simply stop buying it and say nothing at all.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (C) makes the opening claim about customer behaviour. Sentence (D) expands the claim by saying what customers do instead. Sentence (A) uses 'therefore' to draw the inference for companies. Sentence (B) suggests the remedy and ends the paragraph. The coherent order is therefore C-D-A-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) Outrage attracts attention more reliably than agreement does.
(B) Platforms rank posts by the attention they are likely to attract.
(C) Users conclude that the public is more divided than it actually is.
(D) That belief, repeated often enough, begins to make itself true.
(E) The ranking therefore promotes the angriest version of every discussion.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (D) closes with the self-fulfilling consequence of 'That belief', which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (B) describes how platforms rank posts. The full coherent order is B-A-E-C-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) The repeated question restores a choice that the original consent quietly removed.
(B) The same permission, once granted, continues to apply when the application is idle.
(C) A fitness application asks for access to a user's location in order to map runs.
(D) A record therefore accumulates of every place the user visits, running or not.
(E) Most users never revisit the permission screen after the first day.
(F) Operating systems have begun asking again after a few weeks of background use.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) notes the user behaviour that makes it worse, and sentence (F) describes the response from operating systems, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order C-B-D-E-F-A the pair E-F stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Who benefits from a price rule depends almost entirely on who already holds the asset.
(B) Owners, unable to raise rents, spent less on maintenance each year.
(C) Existing tenants benefited immediately and many stayed for decades.
(D) A city introduced rent control to keep older neighbourhoods affordable.
(E) The policy protected those already inside while raising the barrier for everyone outside.
(F) New construction shifted to segments the rules did not cover.
(G) Families arriving in the city found almost nothing available to rent at all.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (D) opens with the policy and its intention. Sentence (C) reports the immediate benefit to existing tenants. Sentence (B) describes the owners' response. Sentence (F) describes the shift in new construction. Sentence (G) reports the effect on newcomers. Sentence (E) summarises the distributional outcome. Sentence (A) states the general conclusion. The coherent order is therefore D-C-B-F-G-E-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Over generations the smaller gene pools make both groups more vulnerable to disease.
(B) Each half then breeds only within itself.
(C) Monitoring cameras in Karnataka have recorded elephants using such crossings within months.
(D) Underpasses and canopy bridges restore the movement the road removed.
(E) A highway cutting through a forest divides one animal population into two.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (E) states the effect of the highway. Sentence (B) describes the breeding consequence with 'Each half then'. Sentence (A) explains the long-term genetic risk. Sentence (D) introduces the engineering remedy. Sentence (C) supplies the supporting evidence and closes. The coherent order is therefore E-B-A-D-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (D)?
(A) Attendance improved immediately, since each test carried marks.
(B) Teachers, however, found themselves setting and marking four times as often.
(C) A college replaced its three-hour final examination with four short tests spread across the term.
(D) Students reported less anxiety than they had felt before the single long paper.
(E) The reform succeeded for the learners and failed for the staff who had to sustain it.
(F) Several reused questions, and the papers soon began to circulate among students.
(G) Any change to assessment must therefore be costed in teacher hours before it is announced.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) adds the effect on students' anxiety, so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (A) reports the first effect on attendance and provides it. Hence (A) immediately precedes (D), and the complete order is C-A-D-B-F-E-G.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (4). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) An average conceals as much as it reveals. (2) Two classes with the same mean score may be completely different places to teach. (3) In the other, half the class is failing while the rest score full marks. (4) Reporting the spread alongside the mean is therefore not a technicality but a necessity.
Removed sentence: In one, nearly every student is close to the average.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence describes the first class with 'In one'. It must therefore come after the sentence that introduces the two classes that illustrate it and before the sentence that describes the contrasting class with 'In the other'. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: An average conceals as much as it reveals. Two classes with the same mean score may be completely different places to teach. In one, nearly every student is close to the average. In the other, half the class is failing while the rest score full marks. Reporting the spread alongside the mean is therefore not a technicality but a necessity.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) Its value lies not in sounding plausible but in being capable of failing a test.
(B) If no observation could possibly contradict a claim, the claim lies outside science.
(C) This is why astrologers, who can explain every outcome after the event, persuade so few scientists.
(D) A hypothesis is a testable statement about how something in the world behaves.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (C) begins with 'This is why' and offers the illustrative case, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (D) defines the key term and must stand first. The full coherent order is D-A-B-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) Competing on the experience, rather than on price, was the move that worked.
(B) A chain of bookshops watched its sales fall as online retailers expanded.
(C) Its first response was to match the discounts offered on the internet.
(D) People came for the afternoon and bought books on the way out.
(E) The chain then rebuilt its shops around readings, children's hours and a café.
(F) Margins collapsed without bringing the customers back.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (B) opens with the problem facing the chain, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (C) describes the first response. The full coherent order is B-C-F-E-D-A.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (4). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) A robot arm can repeat the same weld ten thousand times without tiring. (2) Tasks that humans find effortless often involve judgements no sensor captures easily. (3) Factories therefore automate the repetitive motion and leave the fiddly handling to people. (4) The result is a shared workspace rather than the empty factory once predicted.
Removed sentence: Ask it to pick up a crumpled cloth, however, and it struggles badly.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence contrasts with the difficult task using 'however'. It must therefore come after the sentence that states what the robot does well and before the sentence that explains the underlying reason. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: A robot arm can repeat the same weld ten thousand times without tiring. Ask it to pick up a crumpled cloth, however, and it struggles badly. Tasks that humans find effortless often involve judgements no sensor captures easily. Factories therefore automate the repetitive motion and leave the fiddly handling to people. The result is a shared workspace rather than the empty factory once predicted.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) Drainage built for the older pattern is overwhelmed within an hour of such a burst.
(B) A warmer atmosphere holds more water vapour than a cooler one.
(C) Rainfall records in many districts now show fewer rainy days but heavier downpours.
(D) That extra moisture has to fall somewhere, and it usually falls in concentrated bursts.
(E) Adapting the city, not merely predicting the storm, has become the urgent task.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (C) presents the evidence from rainfall records, and sentence (A) describes the consequence for drainage designed for the older pattern, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order B-D-C-A-E the pair C-A stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) That belief, repeated often enough, begins to make itself true.
(B) Users conclude that the public is more divided than it actually is.
(C) The ranking therefore promotes the angriest version of every discussion.
(D) Outrage attracts attention more reliably than agreement does.
(E) Platforms rank posts by the attention they are likely to attract.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (E) describes how platforms rank posts. Sentence (D) states the fact about outrage that the ranking exploits. Sentence (C) combines the two with 'therefore' to describe the outcome. Sentence (B) reports the impression users form. Sentence (A) closes with the self-fulfilling consequence of 'That belief'. The coherent order is therefore E-D-C-B-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (A)?
(A) Each addition seems harmless when considered on its own.
(B) Every system acquires features faster than it acquires the capacity to support them.
(C) The hidden complexity remains, waiting to surface as the next maintenance problem.
(D) Removing a feature, however, angers the small group that depends on it.
(E) Teams therefore keep everything and hide the complexity behind defaults.
(F) Together, they produce a product whose settings page nobody can navigate.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (A) explains why each addition is accepted. The sentence that continues this thread is (F), which describes the cumulative effect with 'Together'. No other sentence links back to (A) so directly. The complete order is B-A-F-D-E-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Learning was expected to happen after the day's delivery targets had been met.
(B) Completion rose to sixty per cent without a single new course being purchased.
(C) Completion rates after six months stood at four per cent.
(D) A company bought licences to an online course library for all its engineers.
(E) The following year two hours a week were blocked in the calendar for study.
(F) The courses were good; the difficulty was that nobody had been given time for them.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (D) opens with the company's purchase. Sentence (C) reports the disappointing result. Sentence (F) diagnoses the real problem. Sentence (A) explains the expectation that caused it. Sentence (E) describes the change made the following year. Sentence (B) reports the outcome that closes the paragraph. The coherent order is therefore D-C-F-A-E-B.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.
(A) Helmets must conform to national safety standards.
(B) The deaths continued at the same rate through the following year.
(C) Helmet use in that group was found to be close to zero.
(D) Enforcement after dark, not resurfacing, turned out to be the measure that mattered.
(E) A district recorded a sudden rise in road accident deaths among young men.
(F) A closer study of the hospital records showed that most crashes happened after midnight.
(G) Officials first blamed poor road surfaces and ordered repairs.
questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (E) opens with the observed problem; then the rest develop the same point in the order E-G-B-F-C-D. Sentence (A) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Every one of those operations had added cost to an item destined for the scrap bin.
(B) A factory measured defects only at the final inspection stage.
(C) By then a faulty component had already passed through nine operations.
(D) Moving the checks upstream reduced the waste long before the assembly line was redesigned.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (B) describes the factory's original practice. Sentence (C) points out what had happened 'By then'. Sentence (A) spells out the cost of 'those operations'. Sentence (D) reports the corrective action and its result. The coherent order is therefore B-C-A-D.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) Twenty compliant discharges can still exhaust the oxygen the water contains.
(B) The standard, however, applies to a single outlet rather than to the river.
(C) Each plant discharges water that comfortably meets the prescribed standard.
(D) Fish disappear from a stretch in which every permit has been honoured.
(E) Limits set for the whole stretch would prevent what limits per outlet cannot.
(F) A river running through a city receives treated effluent from several plants.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (F) introduces the river and the discharges, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (C) states that each plant meets the standard. The full coherent order is F-C-B-A-D-E.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.
(A) The same people will not cross the road to save two hundred rupees on a refrigerator.
(B) People will drive across town to save two hundred rupees on a kettle.
(C) Money, it turns out, is judged in percentages rather than in rupees.
(D) What differs is the proportion of the price that the saving represents.
(E) The amount saved is identical in both cases.
(F) Household appliance sales rise during the festive quarter.
questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (B) gives the first half of the comparison; then the rest develop the same point in the order B-A-E-D-C. Sentence (F) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (5). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) A small firm making bicycle frames received an order ten times its usual size. (2) Output rose, but so did the proportion of frames rejected at inspection. (3) The new welders had been trained for three days instead of the usual three months. (4) Quality recovered only after the experienced staff were moved into training roles. (5) Capacity, the owner concluded, is limited by skill long before it is limited by equipment.
Removed sentence: The owner hired extra welders and bought two additional machines.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence describes the owner's first response. It must therefore come after the sentence that opens the narrative with the unusually large order and before the sentence that reports the mixed result with 'but'. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: A small firm making bicycle frames received an order ten times its usual size. The owner hired extra welders and bought two additional machines. Output rose, but so did the proportion of frames rejected at inspection. The new welders had been trained for three days instead of the usual three months. Quality recovered only after the experienced staff were moved into training roles. Capacity, the owner concluded, is limited by skill long before it is limited by equipment.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) His neighbours, seeing the lower electricity bills, asked to borrow the sensors the following season.
(B) A farmer in Vidarbha installed soil moisture sensors in two of his cotton fields.
(C) After he adjusted the schedule, his pump ran for half the earlier number of hours.
(D) The readings showed that he had been watering the crop twice as often as it needed.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (A) concludes with the effect on the neighbours, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (B) opens the narrative with the farmer and his action. The full coherent order is B-D-C-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Reviews complaining about this appeared within weeks of the launch.
(B) Honest advertising, the episode suggested, cannot compensate for an awkward design.
(C) The company's first reaction was to add a warning line to the advertisement.
(D) A furniture company advertised a sofa that could be assembled in fifteen minutes.
(E) Complaints continued, because the difficulty lay in the product rather than the description.
(F) Customers found the claim accurate only if two people worked together.
(G) A redesigned bracket allowed a single person to hold the frame while fixing it.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (D) opens with the advertised claim. Sentence (F) reports the customers' experience of 'the claim'. Sentence (A) describes the reviews that followed. Sentence (C) reports the company's first reaction. Sentence (E) explains why complaints continued. Sentence (G) describes the eventual engineering fix. Sentence (B) states the concluding lesson. The coherent order is therefore D-F-A-C-E-G-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the OPENING of the paragraph?
(A) Students who think this way stop attempting problems they cannot solve immediately.
(B) Teaching that mistakes are part of the method changes the assumption, and with it the outcome.
(C) Those who treat difficulty as normal keep working and eventually succeed.
(D) That belief makes a wrong answer feel like evidence about the self.
(E) Many students believe mathematics is a subject you are either born for or not.
(F) The difference in results looks like talent but begins as an assumption.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) states the common belief and needs no earlier sentence, so it opens the passage. Sentence (D) explains the effect of 'That belief', which attaches it directly to the opening sentence. The complete order is E-D-A-C-F-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) Rebuilding them turned out to cost less than the sea wall the town had considered.
(B) Saplings planted along the shore took four years to form a usable barrier.
(C) The mangroves had absorbed exactly that kind of surge for decades.
(D) A coastal town lost a stretch of mangroves to a new seafront promenade.
(E) The promenade was popular and brought visitors throughout the year.
(F) Three seasons later an unusually high tide flooded the market behind it.
(G) The town now treats the greenbelt as infrastructure rather than as scenery.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (G) closes with the change in the town's attitude, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (D) opens with the loss of the mangroves. The full coherent order is D-E-F-C-A-B-G.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) In one, nearly every student is close to the average.
(B) In the other, half the class is failing while the rest score full marks.
(C) Reporting the spread alongside the mean is therefore not a technicality but a necessity.
(D) Two classes with the same mean score may be completely different places to teach.
(E) An average conceals as much as it reveals.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (E) states the opening claim about averages. Sentence (D) introduces the two classes that illustrate it. Sentence (A) describes the first class with 'In one'. Sentence (B) describes the contrasting class with 'In the other'. Sentence (C) draws the conclusion about reporting spread. The coherent order is therefore E-D-A-B-C.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (4). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) Solar panels generate most of their power in the middle of the day. (2) This mismatch leaves cheap afternoon electricity with nowhere useful to go. (3) Storage, whether in batteries or in pumped water, shifts the surplus to the evening. (4) The cost of that shift, rather than the cost of the panel, now decides the economics.
Removed sentence: Household demand, by contrast, peaks in the evening when people return home.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence contrasts it with demand using 'by contrast'. It must therefore come after the sentence that states when solar power is produced and before the sentence that names the resulting problem as 'This mismatch'. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: Solar panels generate most of their power in the middle of the day. Household demand, by contrast, peaks in the evening when people return home. This mismatch leaves cheap afternoon electricity with nowhere useful to go. Storage, whether in batteries or in pumped water, shifts the surplus to the evening. The cost of that shift, rather than the cost of the panel, now decides the economics.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which option correctly gives the FIRST and the LAST sentences of the paragraph, in that order?
(A) Because the warning creates panic, even careful employees sometimes respond without checking the sender's address.
(B) A typical message warns that an account will be closed unless the user verifies it immediately.
(C) The attacker's aim is to make the reader reveal a password or click a harmful link.
(D) Phishing is an attack in which a fraudulent message is disguised as a trustworthy one.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) defines the term 'phishing' and so must come first and therefore opens the paragraph, while sentence (A) begins with 'Because the warning', which can only refer to the warning described in the example and therefore closes it. The complete order is D-C-B-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) It may be checking only the cases the developer already had in mind.
(B) A test suite that never fails is usually telling you nothing.
(C) Deliberately introducing a fault and watching whether the suite notices is a useful audit.
(D) If the tests still pass, the suite needs work before the product does.
(E) Real defects hide in the inputs nobody thought to write down.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) states where real defects actually hide, and sentence (C) proposes the audit technique, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order B-A-E-C-D the pair E-C stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which option correctly gives the FIRST and the LAST sentences of the paragraph, in that order?
(A) A record therefore accumulates of every place the user visits, running or not.
(B) The repeated question restores a choice that the original consent quietly removed.
(C) The same permission, once granted, continues to apply when the application is idle.
(D) A fitness application asks for access to a user's location in order to map runs.
(E) Operating systems have begun asking again after a few weeks of background use.
(F) Most users never revisit the permission screen after the first day.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) introduces the application and the permission it requests and therefore opens the paragraph, while sentence (B) explains why the response matters and closes and therefore closes it. The complete order is D-C-A-F-E-B.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.
(A) As renewable generation grows, however, the same car becomes cleaner without any change to it.
(B) The emissions associated with it occur instead at the power station that charges it.
(C) An electric car produces no exhaust on the street where it is driven.
(D) In a grid dominated by coal, the saving is therefore smaller than the silence suggests.
(E) Its environmental record is tied less to the vehicle than to the grid behind it.
(F) Battery prices have fallen by nearly ninety per cent since 2010.
questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (C) states the visible advantage of the electric car; then the rest develop the same point in the order C-B-D-A-E. Sentence (F) mentions a detail that no other sentence takes up and that breaks the line of thought, so it is the one to be removed.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) A company that does not yet know its customer simply reaches the wrong market faster.
(B) Investment, however, buys speed rather than direction.
(C) A founder with a working prototype is usually advised to raise money quickly.
(D) The months before funding are the cheapest time to discover a mistake.
(E) Capital raised after those conversations buys far more than capital raised before them.
(F) Each conversation with a potential buyer costs nothing and eliminates a wrong assumption.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (C) states the usual advice given to founders, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (B) qualifies that advice with 'however'. The full coherent order is C-B-A-D-F-E.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (B)?
(A) Fewer than a third met the standard the question had described.
(B) A survey asked respondents whether they exercised regularly.
(C) Respondents were not lying; they were reporting the person they intended to be.
(D) Fitness trackers worn by the same group told a very different story.
(E) Eighty per cent said that they did.
(F) Questions about habits therefore measure self-image as much as behaviour.
(G) Where accuracy matters, observation has to supplement what people say about themselves.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (B) introduces the survey question. The sentence that continues this thread is (E), which reports the self-reported answer. No other sentence links back to (B) so directly. The complete order is B-E-D-A-C-F-G.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) The resulting document saves paper and loses readers.
(B) A page of text with no margins feels exhausting to read.
(C) Clients, paying by the page, frequently ask for that space to be filled.
(D) The eye needs a resting edge as much as it needs the letters themselves.
(E) Designers treat empty space as an element rather than as waste.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (A) closes with the ironic outcome, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (B) states the effect of a page without margins. The full coherent order is B-D-E-C-A.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (4). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) A beginner practises a difficult passage by playing it faster and faster. (2) Speed, however, only repeats the mistakes already present in the fingers. (3) The hand then learns one version of the passage rather than several competing ones. (4) Tempo, added afterwards, costs far less effort than correction does.
Removed sentence: Teachers insist instead on slow repetition until the movement is exactly right.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence reports what teachers recommend 'instead'. It must therefore come after the sentence that criticises that method with 'however' and before the sentence that explains the benefit with 'The hand then learns'. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: A beginner practises a difficult passage by playing it faster and faster. Speed, however, only repeats the mistakes already present in the fingers. Teachers insist instead on slow repetition until the movement is exactly right. The hand then learns one version of the passage rather than several competing ones. Tempo, added afterwards, costs far less effort than correction does.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately AFTER sentence (D)?
(A) The cost of that shift, rather than the cost of the panel, now decides the economics.
(B) This mismatch leaves cheap afternoon electricity with nowhere useful to go.
(C) Solar panels generate most of their power in the middle of the day.
(D) Household demand, by contrast, peaks in the evening when people return home.
(E) Storage, whether in batteries or in pumped water, shifts the surplus to the evening.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) contrasts it with demand using 'by contrast'. The sentence that continues this thread is (B), which names the resulting problem as 'This mismatch'. No other sentence links back to (D) so directly. The complete order is C-D-B-E-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come FIRST in the paragraph?
(A) Questions become softer for a candidate who has made a good start and sharper for one who has not.
(B) Firms that adopted them report noticeably better agreement between interviewers.
(C) Most interview panels decide about a candidate within the first few minutes.
(D) Structured interviews, in which every candidate faces the same questions in the same order, limit this drift.
(E) The remainder of the conversation is often spent looking for reasons to justify that impression.
questions.explanationText: The opening sentence must introduce the subject without depending on anything said earlier. Sentence (C) opens with the finding about early decisions, whereas each of the other sentences looks backward: for example (E) describes how the rest of the interview is used. The full coherent order is C-E-A-D-B.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (B)?
(A) The new welders had been trained for three days instead of the usual three months.
(B) Output rose, but so did the proportion of frames rejected at inspection.
(C) Quality recovered only after the experienced staff were moved into training roles.
(D) The owner hired extra welders and bought two additional machines.
(E) A small firm making bicycle frames received an order ten times its usual size.
(F) Capacity, the owner concluded, is limited by skill long before it is limited by equipment.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (B) reports the mixed result with 'but', so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (D) describes the owner's first response and provides it. Hence (D) immediately precedes (B), and the complete order is E-D-B-A-C-F.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which pair of sentences, in the given order, forms the CONCLUSION of the paragraph?
(A) A claim repeated a thousand times therefore carries no more evidence than it did the first time.
(B) A forwarded message gains credibility each time it is forwarded again.
(C) Readers assume that something seen from several contacts must have been checked by someone.
(D) In reality every one of those contacts made exactly the same assumption.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (D) corrects the assumption with 'In reality', and sentence (A) states the conclusion that follows with 'therefore', which settles the passage and leaves nothing hanging. Together they close the paragraph, whose full order is B-C-D-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) Much of this knowledge is informal and is never written down in any manual.
(B) A new employee usually spends the first few weeks simply learning how decisions are made.
(C) Teams that ignore this hidden curriculum often wonder why capable recruits take so long to contribute.
(D) It is picked up in corridor conversations, review meetings and casual lunchtime remarks.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (C) draws the practical lesson for teams and closes the paragraph, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (B) introduces the new employee and the period of learning. The full coherent order is B-A-D-C.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) Completion rates after six months stood at four per cent.
(B) The following year two hours a week were blocked in the calendar for study.
(C) A company bought licences to an online course library for all its engineers.
(D) Learning was expected to happen after the day's delivery targets had been met.
(E) The courses were good; the difficulty was that nobody had been given time for them.
(F) Completion rose to sixty per cent without a single new course being purchased.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (F) reports the outcome that closes the paragraph, which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (C) opens with the company's purchase. The full coherent order is C-A-E-D-B-F.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (G), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) Students reported less anxiety than they had felt before the single long paper.
(B) A college replaced its three-hour final examination with four short tests spread across the term.
(C) Teachers, however, found themselves setting and marking four times as often.
(D) Any change to assessment must therefore be costed in teacher hours before it is announced.
(E) The reform succeeded for the learners and failed for the staff who had to sustain it.
(F) Several reused questions, and the papers soon began to circulate among students.
(G) Attendance improved immediately, since each test carried marks.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) evaluates the reform from both sides, and sentence (D) states the general principle that closes the passage, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order B-G-A-C-F-E-D the pair E-D stands together.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (4). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?
(1) A hill town that attracts visitors soon attracts hotels as well. (2) Each new building draws water from the same small set of springs. (3) Tankers then bring water up the hill at a price residents can hardly afford. (4) The town's popularity ends up taxing precisely the people who made it worth visiting.
Removed sentence: During the peak season the springs cannot meet both local and visitor demand.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence states the shortfall during the peak season. It must therefore come after the sentence that explains the demand that 'Each new building' creates and before the sentence that describes the response with 'Tankers then'. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: A hill town that attracts visitors soon attracts hotels as well. Each new building draws water from the same small set of springs. During the peak season the springs cannot meet both local and visitor demand. Tankers then bring water up the hill at a price residents can hardly afford. The town's popularity ends up taxing precisely the people who made it worth visiting.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which of the following pairs must appear together, in the given order, with the second sentence immediately following the first?
(A) Pressure cookers restore the lost heat by raising the pressure artificially.
(B) Rice simmered at that reduced temperature stays hard long after the stated time.
(C) A recipe that works in Chennai may fail in Shimla without a single error by the cook.
(D) The hill kitchen therefore depends on a device the coastal kitchen can ignore.

questions.explanationText: Sentence (A) introduces the device that solves the problem, and sentence (D) concludes with the comparison between the two kitchens, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order C-E-B-A-D the pair A-D stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (E), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.

The coherent order is therefore C-B-A-D-E.

questions.questionText:

(B) Both reactions are correct, because buyers and sellers read the same number differently.
(C) A sudden fall in the price of onions delights shoppers in the market.
(D) Policies that please one group almost always irritate the other.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (A) contrasts it with the producer's view of 'the same fall', and sentence (B) reconciles the two views, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order C-A-B-D the pair A-B stands together.

questions.questionText:
All but one of the sentences below form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not belong and should be removed.

(E) Today many of them are busier as places to sit, study and use the internet.
questions.explanationText: The remaining sentences form a connected passage: (C) describes the traditional role of libraries; then the rest develop the same point in the order C-E-A-B. questions.questionText:

(B) A single striking experiment proves very little on its own.
(C) Replication, unglamorous as it is, does most of the quiet work of science.
(D) Chance alone will produce an impressive result now and then.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (A) introduces the corrective step with 'Only when', and sentence (C) names and evaluates that step as a closing generalisation, so the second cannot be separated from the first. The other pairs offered break this link or reverse it. In the complete order B-D-A-C the pair A-C stands together.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come immediately BEFORE sentence (B)?
(A) Schools responded rationally to the measure they were being judged by.
(B) Average marks rose, and the policy was declared a success.
(C) A state government decided to measure schools by their board examination results.
(D) Weaker students were quietly discouraged from appearing for the examination at all.
(E) The children who had been excluded, however, appeared in no statistic whatsoever.
(F) A measure that can be improved by removing the difficult cases measures very little.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (B) reports the apparent success, so it needs a sentence before it that supplies exactly that reference. Sentence (D) describes the specific tactic adopted and provides it. Hence (D) immediately precedes (B), and the complete order is C-A-D-B-E-F.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (F), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Choose the option that gives the correct sequence.
(A) Capital raised after those conversations buys far more than capital raised before them.
(B) Each conversation with a potential buyer costs nothing and eliminates a wrong assumption.
(C) A founder with a working prototype is usually advised to raise money quickly.
(D) A company that does not yet know its customer simply reaches the wrong market faster.
(E) The months before funding are the cheapest time to discover a mistake.
(F) Investment, however, buys speed rather than direction.
questions.explanationText: Reading the sentences for their links: sentence (C) states the usual advice given to founders. Sentence (F) qualifies that advice with 'however'. Sentence (D) explains the danger for a company without a known customer. Sentence (E) points to the value of the pre-funding months. Sentence (B) explains why with the cost of each conversation. Sentence (A) closes by comparing capital raised before and after. The coherent order is therefore C-F-D-E-B-A.

questions.questionText:
The sentences given below, labelled (A) to (D), form a coherent paragraph when arranged in the correct order. Which sentence should come LAST in the paragraph?
(A) It also reveals, inadvertently, when a family wakes up and when the house is empty.
(B) This stream of readings lets the utility predict demand with far greater accuracy.
(C) Rules on who may keep such records, and for how long, have not kept pace with the devices.
(D) A smart meter reports household electricity use to the utility every few minutes.
questions.explanationText: The closing sentence must round the passage off rather than open a new line of thought. Sentence (C) concludes on the regulatory gap concerning 'such records', which can only come after the rest of the passage has been laid out; by contrast (D) introduces the smart meter and what it reports. The full coherent order is D-B-A-C.

questions.questionText:
In the paragraph below the sentences are numbered (1) to (3). The sentence given after the paragraph has been removed from it. At which position should it be inserted?

(3) Several institutions have therefore begun to add project reviews and code walkthroughs to their evaluation schemes.
Removed sentence: This method rewards memory far more than it rewards the ability to build something that works.
questions.explanationText: The removed sentence comments on that practice using 'This method', which must point back to the examination system. It must therefore come after the sentence that states the existing practice in neutral, general terms and needs no earlier sentence and before the sentence that illustrates the weakness with a concrete student example. Restoring it at that point gives the original sequence, in which the paragraph runs: Most engineering colleges still assess students mainly through written examinations. This method rewards memory far more than it rewards the ability to build something that works. A student who can reproduce a sorting algorithm on paper may still be unable to debug a simple program. Several institutions have therefore begun to add project reviews and code walkthroughs to their evaluation schemes.

questions.questionText:

(A) Those depending on rainfall harvested less than they had with their old seed.

(F) Advice that travels with the seed matters as much as the seed itself.

(E) While relations are cordial, nobody consults the document at all.
questions.explanationText: Sentence (E) describes what happens while relations are good. The sentence that continues this thread is (C), which explains when 'Its clauses' actually matter. No other sentence links back to (E) so directly. The complete order is B-E-C-D-A.

questions.questionText:

Cold storage near the farm would preserve most of what is currently discarded. Such storage, however, requires reliable electricity in precisely the places that lack it. Food waste in rural areas is therefore an energy problem disguised as an agricultural one.

questions.questionText:
